name: @backthread/ci
description: The Backthread CI-extraction client and its wire contract — extract a repository's structural graph on your own runner and post it, without ever sending source. Includes the ingress's own acceptance gate, so what is accepted is readable rather than asserted.
author: Backthread
comment_files: `src` ships alongside `dist` ON PURPOSE. The whole argument for publishing the acceptance gate is that what we accept becomes readable; a reader who has to de-compile `dist` to check it has been given the letter of that and not the substance. The tests ship for the same reason — a gate whose tests are invisible is a claim, not evidence.
comment_test_isolation: `--experimental-test-isolation=none` runs the test files in one process instead of forking one child per file. Not a speed tweak: the forked runner rebuilds its report by parsing each child's stdout, which misframes across pipe-chunk boundaries and fails with `Unable to deserialize cloned data` against a test file that passed. Full reasoning and the trade-off in .github/workflows/ci.yml.
